newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil court again delays telecom ruling.
newsitem.headline: Brazil court again delays telecom ruling.

text.p: Brazil's highest court put off for a second time a decision on the constitutionality of a law that would lay the groundwork for deregulation of the telecommunications sector, a spokeswoman said.
The spokeswoman for the Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF) said the judgement had been postponed until next week and would probably take place on Wednesday, March 19.
She gave no reason for the postponement except to say there were other more pressing issues on the court's agenda.

The court's decision is anxiously awaited by investors in Brazil state telecom holding Telebras, as a ruling against the law's constitutionality would delay for several months government plans to open up the multi-billion telecom sector.

The same ruling could also suspend the upcoming tender for B Band cellular phone concessions. The tender is scheduled for April 7 and has drawn the interest of some of the biggest names in global telecommunications.
